A lightweight aggregate vehicle model turns terrain, traction, slip, range, and upgrades into vehicle-speed response. It does not simulate individual wheel suspension or wheel-by-wheel drivetrain forces.

01

Powertrain

Throttle, speed, traction, and bogged-load estimates drive acceleration, RPM, and engine/clutch heat. Selectable high/low range changes the response; 4×4 and upgrade state modify aggregate traction. Gear display is a simplified readout, not a component-by-component gearbox simulation.

ENGINE / CLUTCH HEAT · STALL / RESTART
02

Drivetrain upgrades

Portal axles, transfer case, lockers, and shafts are represented as build upgrades that adjust vehicle stats or unlock controls. There is no wheel-speed parity, shaft-stress, or hard-turn binding simulation. Differential lock is a single aggregate traction toggle.

UPGRADE TREE · 4×4 · HIGH / LOW · DIFF LOCK
03

Tyres & pressure

When CTIS is installed, switch between 30 and 18 PSI. Lower pressure and tyre upgrades adjust aggregate traction on soft ground; slip gradually wears the tyre condition. Individual tyre deformation, punctures, bead failure, and heat are not modeled.

30 PSI · 18 PSI · AGGREGATE SLIP / WEAR
04

Terrain & water

Driving and wheelspin accumulate persistent rut values in terrain cells; visible tracks and changed traction, drag, and surface readings follow. Water depth affects engine condition and can stall the engine beyond the intake limit. A snorkel raises that limit; sealed ignition reduces crossing wear.

RUTS · TERRAIN RESPONSE · WATER STALL / RESTART
05

Damage & maintenance

Engine, chassis, and tyre condition are aggregate meters. Slip, rough ground, deep water, and overheating can wear them; high engine or clutch temperatures reduce acceleration, with severe heat adding engine wear. Paid field repair restores some condition; there are no separately simulated axle or suspension failures.

ENGINE · CHASSIS · TYRES · TEMPERATURES
06

Recovery

The winch selects a nearby road-map point as its anchor and pulls the vehicle toward it; the upgraded winch increases reach and pull. Emergency recovery relocates the scout to the nearest road point for ₽500. Cable snag, line angle, anchor breakage, battery draw, and cargo loss are not simulated.

WINCH · ROAD ANCHOR · ₽500 EMERGENCY RECOVERY

## Objective
- Expand the existing TAIGA browser prototype into a playable off-road simulation with technical specifications, a UAZ-469 upgrade tree, and a first-three-hours campaign outline.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing project without asking clarifying questions.
- Cover deformable terrain, drivetrain tuning, damage and maintenance, recovery, cockpit and atmosphere, and a classic utility-vehicle roster.
- Save visual-check screenshots as JPEGs no wider than 1280px, and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Adapt the existing prototype with field, workshop, and field-manual views.
- Present the campaign as scouting, bog crossing, ridge beacon, and workshop debrief; fleet entries beyond the UAZ are campaign concepts, not playable vehicles.
- Describe drivetrain simulation accurately as aggregate vehicle speed and traction, not per-wheel behavior.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added rut accumulation and visual rut marks, water-induced engine stalling and timed restart, plus reduced acceleration for low engine condition, stalling, or no fuel.
- Corrected mission title and description mapping; added a distinct completion description and made the completion toast one-shot.
- Added engine/clutch temperature telemetry, thermal simulation, heat-based acceleration penalties and engine wear, and temperature threshold classes.
- Rewrote field-manual simulation claims to distinguish implemented aggregate mechanics from unsupported per-wheel features.

### Active
- Add thermal warning styling and render `campaignBeats` into the empty `#timeline`.
- Run syntax/gameplay checks, verify objective progression and campaign display, then capture and inspect the latest JPEG within the width limit.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add thermal warning styles and render `campaignBeats` in `#timeline`.
2. Run syntax/gameplay checks and verify mission progression and campaign display.
3. Capture a JPEG no wider than 1280px and inspect only that latest screenshot.
4. Summarize changes, tests, assumptions, and limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Simulation, missions, campaign beats, telemetry, controls, and recovery.
- `index.html`: App layout, workshop, field manual, telemetry, and empty `#timeline`.
- `style.css`: App and responsive styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `game.js` and `index.html` are modified, and `style.css` still needs edits. No gameplay checks or screenshots have been run.
- `campaignBeats` is defined in `game.js` but not rendered.
- `player.engineTemp` and `player.clutchTemp` initialize to 82°C and 38°C; thermal simulation and telemetry updates exist.
- The field-manual copy now reflects implemented aggregate vehicle behavior and explicitly notes unsupported wheel-level, component-specific, and advanced recovery mechanics.

Field manual

Learn the machine. Read the ground. Bring the crew and cargo home.

FIELD GUIDE 01—06

Traction is a conversation
with the ground.

TAIGA is a slow, systemic off-road simulation. The terrain remembers every pass; the truck remembers every mistake.

DESIGN PILLAR 01WEIGHT · GRIP · CONSEQUENCE
SIMULATION SPEC 01 / DRIVETRAIN

Torque, not horsepower.

A lightweight aggregate vehicle model turns terrain, traction, slip, range, and upgrades into vehicle-speed response. It does not simulate individual wheel suspension or wheel-by-wheel drivetrain forces.

01

Powertrain

Throttle, speed, traction, and bogged-load estimates drive acceleration, RPM, and engine/clutch heat. Selectable high/low range changes the response; 4×4 and upgrade state modify aggregate traction. Gear display is a simplified readout, not a component-by-component gearbox simulation.

ENGINE / CLUTCH HEAT · STALL / RESTART
02

Drivetrain upgrades

Portal axles, transfer case, lockers, and shafts are represented as build upgrades that adjust vehicle stats or unlock controls. There is no wheel-speed parity, shaft-stress, or hard-turn binding simulation. Differential lock is a single aggregate traction toggle.

UPGRADE TREE · 4×4 · HIGH / LOW · DIFF LOCK
03

Tyres & pressure

When CTIS is installed, switch between 30 and 18 PSI. Lower pressure and tyre upgrades adjust aggregate traction on soft ground; slip gradually wears the tyre condition. Individual tyre deformation, punctures, bead failure, and heat are not modeled.

30 PSI · 18 PSI · AGGREGATE SLIP / WEAR
04

Terrain & water

Driving and wheelspin accumulate persistent rut values in terrain cells; visible tracks and changed traction, drag, and surface readings follow. Water depth affects engine condition and can stall the engine beyond the intake limit. A snorkel raises that limit; sealed ignition reduces crossing wear.

RUTS · TERRAIN RESPONSE · WATER STALL / RESTART
05

Damage & maintenance

Engine, chassis, and tyre condition are aggregate meters. Slip, rough ground, deep water, and overheating can wear them; high engine or clutch temperatures reduce acceleration, with severe heat adding engine wear. Paid field repair restores some condition; there are no separately simulated axle or suspension failures.

ENGINE · CHASSIS · TYRES · TEMPERATURES
06

Recovery

The winch selects a nearby road-map point as its anchor and pulls the vehicle toward it; the upgraded winch increases reach and pull. Emergency recovery relocates the scout to the nearest road point for ₽500. Cable snag, line angle, anchor breakage, battery draw, and cargo loss are not simulated.

WINCH · ROAD ANCHOR · ₽500 EMERGENCY RECOVERY
DOMESTIC FLEET 06 CHASSIS

Built for the long way around.

FIELD GUIDE 01—06

Traction is a conversation
with the ground.

TAIGA is a slow, systemic off-road simulation. The terrain remembers every pass; the truck remembers every mistake.

DESIGN PILLAR 01WEIGHT · GRIP · CONSEQUENCE
SIMULATION SPEC 01 / DRIVETRAIN

Torque, not horsepower.

A lightweight aggregate vehicle model turns terrain, traction, slip, range, and upgrades into vehicle-speed response. It does not simulate individual wheel suspension or wheel-by-wheel drivetrain forces.

01

Powertrain

Throttle, speed, traction, and bogged-load estimates drive acceleration, RPM, and engine/clutch heat. Selectable high/low range changes the response; 4×4 and upgrade state modify aggregate traction. Gear display is a simplified readout, not a component-by-component gearbox simulation.

ENGINE / CLUTCH HEAT · STALL / RESTART
02

Drivetrain upgrades

Portal axles, transfer case, lockers, and shafts are represented as build upgrades that adjust vehicle stats or unlock controls. There is no wheel-speed parity, shaft-stress, or hard-turn binding simulation. Differential lock is a single aggregate traction toggle.

UPGRADE TREE · 4×4 · HIGH / LOW · DIFF LOCK
03

Tyres & pressure

When CTIS is installed, switch between 30 and 18 PSI. Lower pressure and tyre upgrades adjust aggregate traction on soft ground; slip gradually wears the tyre condition. Individual tyre deformation, punctures, bead failure, and heat are not modeled.

30 PSI · 18 PSI · AGGREGATE SLIP / WEAR
04

Terrain & water

Driving and wheelspin accumulate persistent rut values in terrain cells; visible tracks and changed traction, drag, and surface readings follow. Water depth affects engine condition and can stall the engine beyond the intake limit. A snorkel raises that limit; sealed ignition reduces crossing wear.

RUTS · TERRAIN RESPONSE · WATER STALL / RESTART
05

Damage & maintenance

Engine, chassis, and tyre condition are aggregate meters. Slip, rough ground, deep water, and overheating can wear them; high engine or clutch temperatures reduce acceleration, with severe heat adding engine wear. Paid field repair restores some condition; there are no separately simulated axle or suspension failures.

ENGINE · CHASSIS · TYRES · TEMPERATURES
06

Recovery

The winch selects a nearby road-map point as its anchor and pulls the vehicle toward it; the upgraded winch increases reach and pull. Emergency recovery relocates the scout to the nearest road point for ₽500. Cable snag, line angle, anchor breakage, battery draw, and cargo loss are not simulated.

WINCH · ROAD ANCHOR · ₽500 EMERGENCY RECOVERY

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the existing TAIGA browser prototype into a playable off-road simulation with technical specifications, a UAZ-469 upgrade tree, and a first-three-hours campaign outline.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing project without asking clarifying questions.
- Cover deformable terrain, drivetrain tuning, damage and maintenance, recovery, cockpit and atmosphere, and a classic utility-vehicle roster.
- Save visual-check screenshots as JPEGs no wider than 1280px, and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Adapt the existing prototype with field, workshop, and field-manual views.
- Present the campaign as scouting, bog crossing, ridge beacon, and workshop debrief; fleet entries beyond the UAZ are campaign concepts, not playable vehicles.
- Describe drivetrain simulation accurately as aggregate vehicle speed and traction, not per-wheel behavior.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added persistent rut accumulation and visual marks, water-induced engine stalling and timed restart, and reduced acceleration for low engine condition, stalling, or no fuel.
- Corrected mission title and description mapping; added a distinct completion description and made the completion toast one-shot.
- Added engine/clutch temperature telemetry, thermal simulation, heat-based acceleration penalties and engine wear, threshold classes, and warning styling.
- Rewrote field-manual simulation claims to distinguish implemented aggregate mechanics from unsupported per-wheel features.
- Rendered the `campaignBeats` into `#timeline`, with active/completed styling based on objective progress.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Run browser/gameplay checks for objective progression, timeline states, and thermal warnings.
- Capture and inspect the latest JPEG within the 1280px width limit.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run the prototype in a browser and verify campaign display, objective progression, and thermal warning behavior.
2. Capture a JPEG no wider than 1280px and inspect only that latest screenshot.
3. Summarize changes, tests, assumptions, and limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Simulation, missions, campaign timeline rendering, telemetry, controls, and recovery.
- `index.html`: App layout, workshop, field manual, telemetry, and campaign timeline.
- `style.css`: App and responsive styling, including thermal warnings and timeline states.
- `capture.sh`: Existing screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `game.js` and `index.html` were already modified, and `style.css` now also has changes.
- `renderCampaignTimeline()` is called on startup and marks beats active/completed according to completed objectives.
- `player.engineTemp` and `player.clutchTemp` initialize to 82°C and 38°C; thermal simulation and telemetry updates exist.
- The field manual states that wheel-level suspension, wheel-by-wheel drivetrain forces, component-specific failures, and advanced recovery mechanics are not implemented.
